headline: Generative models predict perturbation responses and reconstruct single-cell dynamics
label: Single Cell Perturbation And Dynamics
summary: Flow matching, disentangled VAEs and optimal transport are being used to predict unseen perturbations and recover dynamics from static single-cell data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is generative prediction of perturbation responses. GFM couples knowledge graphs with latent flow matching to predict responses to unseen Perturb-seq perturbations. PertVI disentangles mitotic phase, cell state, batch and treatment effects. scBIG++ predicts full-gene responses to genetic and chemical perturbations via gene-module clustering. LingoCell adds language-linked in silico perturbation across single-cell and spatial data. A second line infers dynamics from snapshots. COATI uses unbalanced synchronized optimal transport to reconstruct coupled scRNA and scATAC trajectories across held-out stages. PhysInfer applies a physics-constrained network to estimate burst size and frequency from static scRNA-seq, and scSLIDE (Cell) orders samples along disease trajectories using density-based sample embeddings. Multimodal joint embeddings are also represented: scHiR pairs scRNA-seq with scHi-C, and Bloom pairs expression with accessibility in mouse brain. Spatial work centres on 3D reconstruction (HIM-INR, THiRST) and spatial imputation or domain parsing (SpaAxFormer, CroSP). scDeepSim supplies controllable ground truth for benchmarking.
